tasks.label: CMake: configure (Debug)
tasks.detail: Configure the build directory with Ninja and the Debug build type.

tasks.label: CMake: configure (pick build type)
tasks.detail: Configure the build directory with a build type of your choice.

tasks.label: CMake: build (Debug)
tasks.detail: Build into ./build. This is the default build task, bound to Ctrl+Shift+B.

tasks.label: CMake: build (verbose)
tasks.detail: Same build, but every compiler command line is printed.

tasks.label: CMake: build (Release)
tasks.detail: Separate build directory so Debug and Release can coexist.

tasks.label: CMake: rebuild from scratch
tasks.detail: Wipes ./build and configures and builds again. Use when CMake cache is stale.
tasks.command: rm -rf build && cmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug && cmake --build build

tasks.label: CMake: clean
tasks.detail: Removes build artefacts, keeps the configuration.

tasks.label: Run: version
tasks.detail: Smoke test that the binary exists and links.

tasks.label: Run: fetch one site (one JSON line)
tasks.detail: The contract the plasmoid uses: one URL in, one JSON object on stdout. Pipe it into jq to look at it.

tasks.label: Run: fetch into a cache directory
tasks.detail: Writes the colour and the grayscale PNG into the given directory and prints their paths, so both copies can be looked at.

tasks.label: Run: offline (cached icon stays)
tasks.detail: Points at a host that does not resolve. ok is false and the cached paths are still reported, which is the state the widget draws grayscale.

tasks.label: Run: fetch and show the cache
tasks.detail: Fetches one site and then lists the cache directory, so the colour and the grayscale copy can be told apart.

tasks.label: Install: local (build + install to ~/.local)
tasks.detail: Configures build-local, builds Release and installs into ~/.local: the showfavicon binary, the icon, the LICENSE and the QML plasmoid package. ShowFavicon has no daemon, so there is no systemd unit and no D-Bus service to install. Testing is off here to keep the install quick; use the Debug build for that. Plasma caches loaded widgets, so restart plasmashell or re-add the widget before expecting a change to show up.
tasks.command: cmake -B build-local -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$HOME/.local" -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF && cmake --build build-local && cmake --install build-local

tasks.label: Install: local (verify)
tasks.detail: Lists what was installed from the manifest cmake wrote, shows which showfavicon the shell resolves, and prints its version through the installed copy. A stale copy earlier on PATH is the usual reason a change seems to have no effect.
tasks.command: test -f build-local/install_manifest.txt && sort -u build-local/install_manifest.txt; echo; echo '=== which showfavicon ==='; which showfavicon; echo; "${env:HOME}/.local/bin/showfavicon" --version

tasks.label: Install: local (uninstall)
tasks.detail: Removes exactly the files cmake recorded in the manifest, the plasmoid package if it was installed with kpackagetool6, and the leftover Python fetcher from the first draft. Nothing outside ~/.local/bin and ~/.local/share is touched. The favicon cache lives in ~/.local/share/showfavicon, which cmake never installed and this never deletes.
tasks.command: kpackagetool6 --type Plasma/Applet --remove com.martin.showfavicon 2>/dev/null; test -f build-local/install_manifest.txt && xargs -r rm -f < build-local/install_manifest.txt && rm -f build-local/install_manifest.txt && rm -f "${env:HOME}/.local/bin/showfavicon-fetch" && echo 'ShowFavicon removed from ~/.local' || echo 'build-local/install_manifest.txt is missing, so there is nothing to remove'

tasks.label: Plasma: reload widget (install + restart plasmashell)
tasks.detail: Installs the current tree into ~/.local and then restarts the shell, which is what makes the panel read the changed QML. Logging out is not needed and would only do the same thing more slowly. Two states have to be told apart, because the obvious command is a silent no-op in one of them. While plasma-plasmashell.service owns the shell, restarting the unit is the clean way and is used. When it does not own it — the shell was started by kstart, which is where a manual reload leaves it — systemctl --user restart answers success, logs 'Started KDE Plasma Workspace' and leaves the running shell untouched: the process it spawns exits at once because org.kde.plasmashell is already owned, the exit status is 0 so Restart=on-failure never retries, and the unit ends up inactive. Measured on Plasma 6.7.5 Wayland on 2026-09-11, four times in the journal and once by hand. So the unit is used only when it is the owner, and the outcome is checked rather than assumed: the task waits a second, looks for the old PID, and replaces the shell by hand if it is still there. It prints both PIDs, which is the only evidence that anything happened. Quitting first and waiting for the process to disappear is deliberate: kstart into a shell that is still shutting down is the one way this comes back to an empty panel.
tasks.command: set before (pgrep -x plasmashell); systemctl --user is-active --quiet plasma-plasmashell.service; and systemctl --user restart plasma-plasmashell.service; and sleep 1; and not contains -- $before (pgrep -x plasmashell); or begin; echo 'plasma-plasmashell.service does not own the shell, replacing plasmashell by hand'; kquitapp6 plasmashell; for i in (seq 40); pgrep -x plasmashell >/dev/null; or break; sleep 0.25; end; kstart plasmashell; end; pgrep -x plasmashell >/dev/null; and echo "plasmashell $before -> "(pgrep -x plasmashell); or echo 'WARNING: no plasmashell is running, the panel is gone'

tasks.label: Plasma: try widget in a window
tasks.detail: Reads the package from disk on every start, so it needs neither an install nor a shell restart. The fastest way to look at a QML change, at the cost of showing the widget in its own window instead of in the panel. Close the window to end the task.

tasks.label: Test: run (ctest)
tasks.detail: Runs the QTest binaries registered with CTest.

tasks.label: Test: build and run
tasks.detail: Full loop: configure, build, then run the tests.

tasks.label: Test: list
tasks.detail: Shows which tests CTest discovered.

tasks.label: Test: run (verbose)
tasks.detail: Same run, but the qInfo lines are shown. That is where the per-site timings, the icon URL that was picked and the cache paths appear.

tasks.label: Test: run one case
tasks.detail: Runs a single test slot, for example testPicksTheBestIconLink or testFallsBackToFaviconIco.

tasks.label: Test: run the CLI contract
tasks.detail: One JSON line on stdout, and the offline result with the cached paths still reported — the part the plasmoid parses.

tasks.label: Test: rerun failed
tasks.detail: Re-runs only the tests that failed in the previous run.

tasks.label: Check: dependencies
tasks.detail: Prints the Qt versions the build relies on, and the CMake that resolves them.
tasks.command: pkg-config --modversion Qt6Core Qt6Network Qt6Gui Qt6Svg Qt6Test; cmake --version | head -n 1

tasks.label: Check: clang-format (dry run)
tasks.detail: Lists files that do not match .clang-format. Needs clang installed.
